selenoprotein synthesis in bacterial pathogens is regulated by host immune system and that selenoprotiens are required for virulence and immune evasion.

the identification, function, and regulation of selenoproteines in bacterial pathogenesis.

the role of selenoprotein in bacterial pathogenesis is still not fully elucidated.

the selenoproteomes of bacteria are highly diverse and are involved in several aspects of bacterial physiology.
selenoprotein expression in bacteria and host cells is critical for bacterial pathogenesis, microbiome composition and host immune response.
